), }, { id: "full", label: "Full answer", readTime: 20, content: ( <>

Why it matters

Uncooked rice can contain spores of Bacillus cereus, which survive cooking. At room temperature they can germinate and produce toxins that reheating won’t destroy.

What experts recommend

  • Cool rice within one hour of cooking
  • Store it in the fridge at or below 5°C
  • Eat leftovers within 24 hours
  • Reheat only once, until steaming hot

The bottom line

If your rice has been out overnight, the safest choice is to throw it away.

/* Coo's art: an illustrated carrier pigeon, his mailbox and his post, as WebP data URIs so
 * one install brings everything. His flight is in coo-fly-art.ts. Sizes and points are in each image's own pixels. */

export const COO_ART = {
  stand:
    "data:image/webp;base64,",
  box: "data:image/webp;base64,",
  boxFlag:
    "data:image/webp;base64,",
  post: "data:image/webp;base64,",
};

export const COO_GEO = {
  /** Every pigeon frame is placed by the middle of his red cap, so swapping frames never jumps. */
  stand: {
    ...{ w: 186, h: 185 },
    cap: { x: 145.7, y: 17.4 },
    feet: { x: 115.8, y: 183 },
    eye: { x: 152.8, y: 38.8, r: 6.6 },
  },
  box: { ...{ w: 110, h: 151 }, foot: { x: 52.8, y: 151 } },
  boxFlag: { ...{ w: 108, h: 166 }, foot: { x: 51.1, y: 166 } },
  post: { w: 41, h: 131 },
  /** His feathers by the eye, for the lid when he blinks. */
  lid: "rgb(124 131 154)",
} as const;

/* Crumb's art: three short eating clips (hungry → content → full → stuffed), cut from an
 * animation into transparent WebP strips, and a cookie, whole and bitten, for the flights.
 * Frame 0 of each strip is the still he starts that clip from; frames 1… are the clip, from
 * the moment the cookie is in his hands. As data URIs so one install brings everything. */

export const CRUMB_ART = {
  strips: [
    "data:image/webp;base64,",
    "data:image/webp;base64,",
    "data:image/webp;base64,",
  ],
  cookie:
    "data:image/webp;base64,",
  bitten:
    "data:image/webp;base64,",
};

export const CRUMB_FRAMES = {
  /** One frame, in image px. */
  w: 134,
  h: 156,
  /** Frames per strip and the rate they play at. */
  count: 19,
  fps: 10,
  /** Where the cookie sits in his hands on frame 1, as fractions of a frame, and its size. */
  hands: { x: 0.5, y: 0.61, size: 0.24 },
} as const;
